description:
# Phase outcome

Jido ships as one target-specific package that contains a private Erlang/OTP runtime. The package provides the TUI, `run`, `eval`, and the optional foreground daemon. Native release jobs publish tested archives, metadata, checksums, notices, signatures, and provenance. Homebrew and Windows channels use the same command and version contract.

# Entry gate

Start implementation after `jido_cli-tqg.5.7`, `jido_cli-tqg.6.2`, and `jido_cli-tqg.6.4` are complete. This keeps release work on the approved immutable GitHub Jidoka dependency after the public API work is stable.

# Source and boundaries

- Use `RELEASE_PLAN.md` as the release contract.
- Keep normal TUI, `run`, and `eval` execution local by default.
- Keep the daemon foreground-only and loopback-only.
- Keep daemon-owned persistence separate from Jidoka session persistence.
- Keep packaged-artifact acceptance separate from local JSONL artifact lifecycle.
- Use the Mix release package path. Keep Burrito only as a fallback for a failed target gate.

# Child tasks

## Release correctness

1. `jido_cli-tqg.7.1` — Use an immutable GitHub Jidoka dependency (P0)
2. `jido_cli-tqg.7.2` — Make the Mix application version the only release version source (P0)
3. `jido_cli-tqg.7.3` — Resolve secure per-user state roots on every platform (P0)

## Daemon and platform boundary

4. `jido_cli-tqg.7.4` — Add the optional daemon application supervision boundary (P0)
5. `jido_cli-tqg.7.5` — Specify the framed daemon wire protocol v1 (P0)
6. `jido_cli-tqg.7.6` — Store daemon authentication and discovery state securely (P0)
7. `jido_cli-tqg.7.7` — Implement the framed loopback daemon client and server (P0)
8. `jido_cli-tqg.7.8` — Persist daemon-owned state and recover after restart (P1)
9. `jido_cli-tqg.7.9` — Route foreground daemon commands without changing local execution (P0)
10. `jido_cli-tqg.7.10` — Define and enforce the daemon work lifecycle and shutdown policy (P0)
11. `jido_cli-tqg.7.11` — Make file, signal, and shell boundaries portable to Windows (P0)

## Package decision and first matrix

12. `jido_cli-tqg.7.12` — Define the isolated artifact and release metadata contract (P0)
13. `jido_cli-tqg.7.13` — Build a hermetic packaged-artifact acceptance harness (P0)
14. `jido_cli-tqg.7.14` — Confirm Mix release packaging on the first target matrix (P0)
15. `jido_cli-tqg.7.15` — Implement the selected private-OTP artifact builder (P0)
16. `jido_cli-tqg.7.16` — Audit bundled dependencies and prepare license notices (P1)
17. `jido_cli-tqg.7.17` — Generate release metadata, checksums, SBOM, and provenance (P1)
18. `jido_cli-tqg.7.18` — Build native unsigned artifacts in a pinned draft-release workflow (P1)
19. `jido_cli-tqg.7.19` — Pass automated packaged acceptance on the first target matrix (P1)
20. `jido_cli-tqg.7.20` — Complete manual TUI acceptance on the first target matrix (P1)

## Services, trust, and later channels

21. `jido_cli-tqg.7.21` — Add Homebrew installation and tap update automation without a service (P1)
22. `jido_cli-tqg.7.22` — Add the Homebrew per-user daemon service (P2)
23. `jido_cli-tqg.7.23` — Add explicit Windows daemon service operations (P2)
24. `jido_cli-tqg.7.24` — Sign and notarize macOS release artifacts (P2)
25. `jido_cli-tqg.7.25` — Sign Windows release executables (P2)
26. `jido_cli-tqg.7.26` — Publish coordinated signed GitHub and Hex releases (P1)
27. `jido_cli-tqg.7.27` — Publish a Scoop manifest for the signed Windows ZIP (P2)
28. `jido_cli-tqg.7.28` — Add Linux ARM64 to the isolated release matrix (P2)
29. `jido_cli-tqg.7.29` — Evaluate Winget and homebrew-core readiness (P3)

# Decision gates

- Protocol v1 and lifecycle policy block transport work.
- The artifact contract blocks the Mix release confirmation.
- The Mix release confirmation blocks builder implementation.
- The full hermetic harness and the builder both block native draft builds.
- The first automated and manual matrices block stable publication.
- macOS and Windows trust work blocks the signed stable pipeline.

# Status rule

All 29 child tasks remain open. Dependency links, not list order or priority alone, control ready work. Manual TUI checks are release gates. They do not replace deterministic automated checks.
